mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points month-over-month signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances where UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where HOUST increases over three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% year-over-year, it signals a restrictive monetary policy combined with weak economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy with weak growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5% and GDPC1 YoY growth < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 month-over-month signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances where PAYEMS increases > 200k MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals increased consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances where RSAFS increases over three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 3% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals accommodative monetary policy combined with a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with strong labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 3% and UNRATE < 4%.
